description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/memory.rs:186-194

```rust
/// Register an account and return `self` for chaining.
pub fn with_account(self, account_id: &str) -> Self {
    self.inner
        .lock()
        .unwrap()
        .accounts
        .insert(account_id.to_owned(), AccountStore::new());
    self
}
```

`HashMap::insert(k, v)` replaces any existing entry. If the caller
chains `MemoryBackend::new().with_account("acc1")` and then later
(perhaps via the cloned `Arc<MemoryBackend>` passed elsewhere) calls
`with_account("acc1")` again — say, as part of a re-setup in a
multi-stage integration test — every node, blob, and change-log
entry under "acc1" is silently destroyed and replaced with a fresh
empty `AccountStore::new()`.

The doc comment says "Register an account and return `self` for
chaining." It does not say "and clear any existing state on
collision". A consumer reading just the doc has no warning.

This is more than a docs gap because the alternative behaviour is
plausible: `HashMap::entry(k).or_insert_with(AccountStore::new)`
would be a no-op on collision and would preserve the existing
state. Without explicit documentation, a caller cannot tell which
semantics they get.

Concrete impact: the test in
`crate-jmap-filenode-server/tests/filenode_tests.rs` constructs a
new `MemoryBackend` per test, so the test suite never hits this
case. A downstream consumer building a multi-stage demo (e.g. a
boot script that registers accounts from a config file and may
re-load on SIGHUP) WILL hit this case.

Suggested fix:

1. Change to `or_insert_with(AccountStore::new)` — preserve existing
   state on collision. Add a sibling `reset_account(&str)` for the
   "destroy and recreate" path if any test actually needs it. This
   is the safer default.
2. OR keep the destructive semantics and document them loudly in the
   doc comment: "Registering an account with an id that already
   exists ERASES the existing account's state." Then add a
   `register_account_idempotent` for the safe path.

Propagation note: canonical sibling
`crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:270-273` (`register_account`)
uses `inner.known_accounts.insert(...)` on a `HashSet`, which is
idempotent for the "is account known" question because HashSet
inserts the same key once. Mail-server does NOT have the same
problem — only filenode-server's nested `AccountStore` (with its own
nodes/state/change-log inside) does. This is a single-crate fix,
not a propagation.

`api-contract,underspecified` because the public method's behaviour
on collision is not documented and the two plausible semantics
diverge silently.
title: MemoryBackend::with_account silently overwrites existing account state — undocumented destructive behaviour
